name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,415

clue.text: Discover the whereabouts of mean talking girl

indicators.note: talking means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: mean is LOW (a low trick) and the girl is KATE; said together they make the answer

explanation.surface: Someone tries to track down a girl with a nasty tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean talking girl' reads as a girl who speaks unkindly, but mean is the adjective low and the girl's name is Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find out exactly where it is, which is discovering its whereabouts.

clue.text: Beat poet finally sharing blame as broadcast

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word poet
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of poet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A beat poet shares blame for something put out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' reads as one phrase, like Ginsberg, but Beat is the definition and poet only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste someone is to thrash them, physically or with fierce criticism, so it means to beat.

clue.text: European intent on jogging in California

indicators.note: jogging jolts things about, so these words are shaken into a fresh order
in places the shaken letters inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CAL is a standard abbreviation for the US state of California

explanation.surface: A determined European goes running in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental describes someone from mainland Europe, as the British say, so it is an adjective or noun for a European.

clue.text: Child framing answer perfectly

indicators.note: framing means the first word surrounds the next one like a picture frame

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A youngster gives exactly the right reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to a T' means exactly or precisely, so it stands in for perfectly.

clue.text: Roman observers primarily unhappy with the Italian transport system

indicators.note: primarily keeps only the first letter of observers
unhappy letters are disturbed and out of sorts, so they are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of observers
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Visitors from Rome grumble about the transport in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monorail is a railway running on a single track, one kind of transport system.

clue.text: Against getting called back to Germany whenever required

indicators.note: called back means the word for called is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: leaning on a wall is leaning against it
named means called, as in given a name
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An opponent is summoned back to Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available on demand is supplied whenever someone asks for it, the moment it is needed.

clue.text: Appear more important than one of Falstaff's recruits on account of earlier

blocks.note: to argue over something is to argue on account of it
Simon Shadow is one of the feeble men Falstaff recruits in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2

explanation.surface: A man seems grander than one of Falstaff's ragged conscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' tells you the phrase for on account of goes in front of the recruit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow someone is to outshine them and make them seem less significant by comparison.

clue.text: Help to get young girl married off

indicators.note: married is abbreviated as one letter, and off says that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a maid is a young unmarried woman
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Assistance is sought to get a young girl wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'married off' sounds like a wedding being arranged; here it means remove the letter for married.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is a direct synonym of help, as a noun or a verb meaning assistance.

clue.text: Delay departure of ship carrying German leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, at the front
a vessel carrying cargo holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
the first letter of German

explanation.surface: A ship's sailing is held up while it takes on a German captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departure of ship' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at departure.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on longer than expected, putting off the moment of leaving.

clue.text: Well-balanced whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: a word that looks the same whichever way you read it, forwards or backwards, is a palindrome

blocks.note: the word meaning even and steady, which reads identically in both directions

explanation.surface: Something is fair and even from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means even and steady, with neither side higher, so it is well-balanced.

clue.text: Girl, not quite eight, reportedly in charge

indicators.note: not quite means the name falls one letter short, losing its end
reportedly means as heard said, so a spoken word stands for a different spelling

blocks.note: a girl's name
the number said out loud matches a past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A little girl, not yet eight, is said to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite eight' reads as an age; not quite actually trims the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official charge or commission given to someone to act.

clue.text: Theologian retaining support for the most part in French city

indicators.note: for the most part means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes
retaining means holding on to, so the first piece keeps the second inside it

blocks.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
a rest is a support, as in an armrest
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A churchman shelters in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' looks like the definition, but French belongs to the wordplay, giving the French for in; the definition is just city, and it is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital city of Saxony in eastern Germany.

clue.text: Enthusiastic writer of sacred songs needing no introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction the name loses its opening letter

blocks.note: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms

explanation.surface: A keen hymn writer is so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' sounds like praise for fame, but it means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and keen, a straightforward synonym of enthusiastic.

clue.text: King on record over letter granting liberty

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the pair preceding is read backwards

blocks.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
an EP is an extended-play record
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A monarch's recorded letter frees someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Permissive means allowing freedom or tolerating behaviour, so it describes something granting liberty.

clue.text: Irate tenor embarrassed over Goossens' opening question

indicators.note: someone embarrassed is flustered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the opening of a name is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of Goossens

explanation.surface: An angry tenor is embarrassed by the conductor's first question.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Goossens was a British conductor, which suits the tenor in the surface; only his initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate is to question someone closely and formally, as police do with a suspect.

clue.text: Check for something done in opposition before

blocks.note: counter means contrary, as in running counter to
an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: A test of something done by the opposing side earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' says the piece for in opposition comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract something is to act against it and neutralise it, which is to check it.

clue.text: Everything left ultimately to a Spartan serf

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word left

blocks.note: the last letter of left
a helot was a serf of ancient Sparta

explanation.surface: Everything is finally bequeathed to a slave in Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the lot' is everyday British speech for all of it, the whole amount.

clue.text: A French girl stripping off to reveal ...

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer layer, so the name loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: une is French for a, feminine form
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A French girl undresses to show off; the dots run on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping off' sounds racy, but it just trims the name at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or bring it to light, which is to reveal it.

clue.text: Angrier after extremely bizarre puzzle

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of bizarre are kept
after places the word for angrier behind the two kept letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of bizarre
wild means furious, so wilder means angrier

explanation.surface: Someone grows angrier after a very strange riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely bizarre' reads as very odd; extremely actually picks the ends of bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to confuse them thoroughly, so the verb puzzle is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Giving full particulars of a notable achievement involving the weaker batsmen

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up inside, so the batsmen sit within the achievement

blocks.note: a deed is a notable act or feat
in cricket the tail is the weaker batsmen who bat last in the order

explanation.surface: A report describes a cricket feat involving the lower-order batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail-enders are the poor batters at the end of the order, usually the bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed account gives full particulars, covering every specific point.

clue.text: ... middle of chest right after rock star's painful blow

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter
after places the letter for chest and the letter for right behind the singer's name

blocks.note: Sting is the English rock singer, formerly of the Police
the central letter of chest
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a rock star takes a painful thump in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a sharp painful blow, one that smarts like a sting.

clue.text: Rough track by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means judging only by what the ear hears, not the spelling

blocks.note: a course is a track, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: A route that sounds bumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture or manner, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Complain endlessly maintaining it's not outside

indicators.note: endlessly means the word is left without its last letter
maintaining means holding, so the shortened word keeps the next one inside

blocks.note: to whine is to complain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly, insisting it is indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Within means inside, the opposite of outside, so not outside is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Somewhere to sit and fish

blocks.note: first meaning: a seat or roost, especially a bird's
second meaning: a freshwater fish with spiny fins

explanation.surface: An angler looks for a spot to settle and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a bird's roost or any high seat, and also the name of a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Filled in after a fashion by chap in woolly

indicators.note: after a fashion means done in some loose way, so the letters are put into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Ed is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A form is completed sloppily by a man in a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like a garment, but it is the adjective meaning vague; in Britain a woolly is a knitted jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly thinking is vague and confused, so woolly means lacking clear outlines or meaning.

clue.text: Artist unknown in part of India

indicators.note: in places the unknown letter inside the name of the Indian state

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
in algebra an unknown is x, y or z

explanation.surface: A painter of no fame is working in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Starts to write report exonerating northern architect

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An inquiry clears an architect from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the English architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: Firm employing a horse and rider for example

definitions.note: names the man by example: the novelist's middle name was Rider

indicators.note: a firm employing someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: hard means firm, not soft
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company takes on a horse and a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' looks like a jockey, but it is a name: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines. The horse and the a both go inside, horse first.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Rider Haggard was the Victorian adventure novelist, so a man called Rider is a Haggard.

clue.text: Musical abridged for a single performance

indicators.note: abridged means cut short, so the title loses its last letter

blocks.note: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical

explanation.surface: A shortened musical is staged for one night only.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single booked performance by musicians or comedians.

clue.text: Plant disease checked by English fellow's universal remedy

indicators.note: checked by means held back by, so the disease is stopped in the middle by the next pieces

blocks.note: leaf curl is a plant disease
E is the abbreviation for English
Al is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: An Englishman finds a miracle treatment for a crop blight.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all is a single remedy said to fix every ailment, a panacea.

clue.text: A right-wing piece about coming first is of little value

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for piece faces the other way
coming first sets the turned word in front of the other pieces

blocks.note: piece is slang for a gun
taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative's contribution is dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests an article or share; in American slang it is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means trifling or having no force, so it describes something of little value.

clue.text: Concerned with finding time to object to plan

blocks.note: to be in something, as in in business, is to be concerned with it
T is the usual abbreviation for time
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone has time on their hands to raise an objection to a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it as a purpose, so the verb plan is a direct synonym.
